calls.head: The Sharks like Dellandrea’s line against Klapka’s
calls.body: At home, the Sharks keep sending Dellandrea’s line (Goodrow, Dellandrea and Ostapchuk) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Warsofsky keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Flames’ fourth line is Tsyplakov, Castagna and Klapka.

CGY.head: We had Calgary as slight underdogs (44%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: Calgary found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Calgary usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots. Not tonight: an 8.6% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 5.5% (about 5.7% against San Jose) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Flames edge the Sharks
paras: Adam Klapka struck first for the Flames midway through the first. William Strömgren, in his fourth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Klapka, midway through the third to make it 2-0, in his first game of the season, and that goal turned out to be the winner. Sam Dickinson pulled the Sharks within one less than three minutes later.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Dustin Wolf made 26 saves for the Flames, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped 20 of 22 at the other end. The Flames improved to 7-8-0 and climbed to fifth in the Pacific, while the Sharks dropped to 7-8-1, fourth in the Pacific.

items.text: Sam Dickinson scored his first goal of the season, his first since Nov 2, 2025 (75 games played since).
